statement: The critical strip norm gives uniform sharp inversion needed for the full prime sum. Every strict logarithmic weakening admits one escaped-center smooth witness defeating the symmetric formula.
compatible_assumptions: Fixed positive strip margin, original value envelopes and local H¹ or literal manuscript (A) for the positive theorem. The smooth witness satisfies literal (A) and (B) on any fixed 0<ε<1/4.
already_proved: Critical sufficiency, per-stage packet gain, and one witness with all negative-log norms finite, zero prime samples, finite arithmetic terms and two incompatible subsequences.
new_claim_suggested: Determine whether a trace formula with a different infinite atomic input admits the same exact logarithmic boundary.
conjectural_or_unresolved: Determine whether a trace formula with a different infinite atomic input admits the same exact logarithmic boundary.
potential_counterexamples: Pointwise inversion at each fixed prime-power argument can hold while the infinite weighted prime sum fails to converge under the contour cutoff.
significance: Closes the universal signed symmetric boundary problem raised in Round 16 within the stated norm scale.
difficulty: The one-witness statement requires stage-specific norm and finite-height budgets in addition to the fixed-prime packet estimate.
next_precise_step: Specify one other arithmetic trace formula and check its contour bounds and atomic coefficients before transferring the construction.
tests: Tilted interpolation, the sharp Dirichlet kernel, good-height contour, and diagonal control of two subsequences.
